James]] | country = United Kingdom | language = English | genre = [[Erotic romance]] | publisher = [[Vintage Books]] | pub_date = 2011–2021 | media_type = Print (paperback) }} '''''Fifty Shades''''' is a series of [[erotic novel]]s by British author [[E. L. James]], initially a [[trilogy]] consisting of ''[[Fifty Shades of Grey]]'' (2011), ''[[Fifty Shades Darker]]'' (2012) and ''[[Fifty Shades Freed]]'' (2012).{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/05/22/books/fifty-shades-of-grey-by-e-l-james-in-demand-at-libraries.html?pagewanted=all|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=21 May 2012|title=Libraries Debate Stocking 'Fifty Shades of Grey' Trilogy|author=Julie Bosman}}{{cite magazine|url=http://entertainment.time.com/2012/03/29/the-shy-british-mum-behind-50-shades-of-grey/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120330212825/http://entertainment.time.com/2012/03/29/the-shy-british-mum-behind-50-shades-of-grey/|url-status=dead|archive-date=30 March 2012|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |title=The Shy British Mum Behind 50 Shades of Grey | date=29 March 2012}} The series traces the deepening relationship between college graduate Anastasia Steele and young businessman Christian Grey. Christian introduces Ana to the world of [[BDSM]]. James has spoken of her shock at the success of the book: "The explosion of interest has taken me completely by surprise."{{cite web|url=http://www.shropshirestar.com/news/2012/07/16/fifty-shades-of-grey-author-e-l-james-exclusive-interview/|title=Fifty Shades of Grey author E L James – Exclusive interview|date=16 July 2012|website=Shropshire Star|accessdate=16 July 2012}} She has described the ''Fifty Shades'' trilogy as "my [[midlife crisis]], writ large. All my fantasies in there, and that's it."{{cite web |url=http://today.msnbc.msn.com/id/47066520/ns/today-books |title='Fifty Shades' author 'stunned' at success of erotic trilogy |publisher=Today MSNBC |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120420041235/http://today.msnbc.msn.com/id/47066520/ns/today-books |archive-date=20 April 2012 |url-status=dead}} She did not start to write until January 2009, as she revealed while still active on [[FanFiction.Net]]: "I started writing in January 2009 after I finished reading the [[Twilight (novel series)|Twilight]] saga, and I haven't stopped since. I discovered Fan Fiction in August 2009. Since then I have written two fics and plan on doing at least one more. After that ... who knows?"{{Cite web |url=http://www.mediabistro.com/galleycat/fifty-shades-of-grey-wayback-machine_b49124 |title=The Lost History of Fifty Shades of Grey |access-date=22 February 2015 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140727045638/http://www.mediabistro.com/galleycat/fifty-shades-of-grey-wayback-machine_b49124 |archive-date=27 July 2014 |url-status=dead }} In August 2013, sales of the trilogy saw James top the ''[[Forbes]]''{{'}} list of the highest-earning authors{{cite web|title=E.L. James Seals A Spot On List of Britain's Richest Authors|url=http://www.themoviefiftyshades.com/e-l-james-earns-over-33m-in-one-year-for-fifty-shades-and-seals-a-spot-on-list-of-britains-richest-author//|publisher=[[Lia]]|access-date=23 June 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714213248/http://www.themoviefiftyshades.com/e-l-james-earns-over-33m-in-one-year-for-fifty-shades-and-seals-a-spot-on-list-of-britains-richest-author//|archive-date=14 July 2014|url-status=dead}} with earnings of $95 million, which included $5 million for the film rights to ''Fifty Shades of Grey''.{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-23681220 | title=Fifty Shades makes EL James top-earning author | work=BBC News | access-date=15 August 2013 | date=13 August 2013}} In spite of the success, the books have also been largely panned by critics,{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/movies/la-et-mn-fifty-shades-darker-trailer-20160913-snap-story.html|title=First 'Fifty Shades Darker' trailer filled with lots of plot, little kissing|last=Hill|first=Libby|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=13 September 2016|access-date=10 February 2017 |quote=The books were critically savaged hot messes that sold over 100 million copies for the sex.}} with the first entry in particular "being ridiculed by virtually every critic who has read it."{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/02/15/movies/fifty-shades-of-grey-the-movie-as-a-fairy-tale.html|title='Fifty Shades of Grey,' the Movie, as a Fairy Tale|last=Lyall|first=Sarah|newspaper=The New York Times|date=11 February 2015|access-date=10 February 2017}} Since 2015 the series has been expanded with a parallel set of novels "as told by Christian": ''[[Grey: Fifty Shades of Grey as Told by Christian|Grey]]'' follows the events of ''Fifty Shades of Grey'' but from the perspective of Christian Grey, ''[[Darker: Fifty Shades Darker as Told by Christian|Darker]]'' (2017) and ''[[Freed: Fifty Shades Freed as Told by Christian|Freed]]'' (2021) do the same for ''Fifty Shades Darker'' and ''Fifty Shades Freed'', respectively.
